name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.171.0 — The review page paints every marked area on its screen previews at all times — a numbered orange pin on the box, the same id on its note row — and the whole row is the click target, so selecting a note lights its box and clicking a box highlights its note. A box belongs to the state it was drawn on, and selecting its note switches the screen to that state. Each board gains an eye toggle that hides its marks, the composer gains a Mark an area action, and a mark now reads as a highlighter tint inside a dashed frame held clear of the content so it can never be mistaken for a border. Addressing a region note re-anchors its box against the edited mock in headless Chrome before the note turns amber, reporting a lost box rather than guessing; the client mount stores and re-places regions, drawing works by long-press on touch, and the atlas index cards carry per-screen open and needs-you counts. 7.170.0 — The design stage prints the work, not the inventory. `design-atlas.js check` collapses its advisory warn lines to one `⚠️ <n> warn(s) — --verbose to list` count and omits the per-screen kit/bespoke breakdown, keeping the running unabsorbed total on every run; `mocks-driver.js notes open` collapses the answered-question history to a count and stops the journey-listed open notes after twenty with a `… <n> more open note(s)` tail. `--verbose` and `--all` restore the full pre-change output byte-for-byte, and no gate, refusal or served page changes behavior. 7.169.0 — A mock-page note can now mark an area: drag a rectangle over any part of a served mock and the note lands on that content at every viewport width, painted in its status colour by the notes layer. The box is stored as a fraction of the smallest element containing it with the covered children as the reflow fallback, so it re-finds its spot or honestly reports itself outdated and offers re-placement. The owner's card beside the box carries accept, reject with a reason, resolve, withdraw and delete behind an undoable toast.
